How to run it
Straight sets: do all the sets of each exercise, rest, then move to the next.
Main Circuit
Front squat
3 sets10 repsBarbell/Rack10kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Rest the bar across the front of the shoulders, elbows lifted high to make a shelf, hands lightly guiding the bar, feet shoulder-width, core braced hard.

Movement: Sit the hips down with an upright torso, elbows kept high, to a comfortable depth, then drive up through the heels to stand tall.

Focus: Keep the elbows up so the chest stays tall and the bar secure, and the knees in line with the middle toes. Keep the heels down and the core braced, and control depth to protect the knees and back.

Romanian deadlift – BB
3 sets8 repsBarbell15kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall with a barbell held at the front of your thighs, hands just outside your legs, feet hip-width. Set the shoulders back, brace the core hard, and keep a soft bend in the knees.

Movement: Push the hips back and slide the bar down the front of your legs, keeping it in contact, until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings. Keep the knees still and the shins vertical. Drive the hips forward to stand tall and finish with the glutes.

Focus: The back stays flat from start to finish, never rounded. This is a hip hinge, not a squat, so the movement happens at the hips while the bar tracks close to the legs. Only lower as far as you can hold a flat back, and don't lean back or over-arch at the top.

Overhead press – standing
3 sets8-10 repsDB or similarModerate
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, ribs down, glutes and core braced.

Movement: Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are straight, then lower back to the shoulders under control.

Focus: Keep the ribs down and squeeze the glutes so the lower back doesn't arch as you press. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears, and press within a comfortable range.

Reverse fly – single arm
3 sets10 repsDB or similar3kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Hinge forward with a flat back, a light dumbbell in one hand hanging below the chest, elbow softly bent, other hand supporting.

Movement: Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height, squeezing the shoulder blade, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep a soft elbow bend and lead with the back of the hand, squeezing the shoulder blade. Keep the back flat and don't swing or shrug, using a light weight.

For your game: Keeping your shoulders and arms in good condition helps you swing freely and without pain.

Seated cable row – close neutral grip
3 sets10 repsCable row machine19.25kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Sit at the low cable, feet braced, a neutral close handle, arms extended, chest up, back tall.

Movement: Pull the handle to the lower abdomen, elbows driving back close to the body, then return slowly under control.

Focus: Drive the elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades, keeping the back tall and still. Keep the shoulders down, and control the return without rocking.

Face pull – cable, with rotation
3 sets10 repsCable machine1.5kg
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand at a cable at head height, a rope in hand, arms extended forward, ribs down, core braced.

Movement: Pull towards the face and rotate the hands so the knuckles finish pointing up and back, elbows high, then return under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbows high and add the rotation from the shoulders, not shrugging. Keep the ribs down and the torso still, and control the return.

For your game: Healthy, stable shoulders keep your swing connected and protect your lead shoulder.

Step-down – single leg
3 sets8 each sideStep boxBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Stand on top of a low step on one leg, the other foot hovering off the edge, arms out for balance.

Movement: Bend the standing knee to lower the free foot slowly towards the floor, lightly tap, then drive back up to stand tall on the one leg.

Focus: Keep the standing knee tracking over the foot, never caving in, and the hips level throughout. Control the lower down slowly, and keep the movement in the standing leg, not by reaching with the free foot.

Dorsiflexion – banded
3 sets10 each sideBandLight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Sit on the floor, working leg straight. Loop a band round the ball of the foot, anchored ahead of you so it pulls the foot away.

Movement: Pull the toes and forefoot back towards the shin against the band, then let it draw the foot slowly back out.

Focus: Keep the knee still and move only at the ankle. The slow return matters as much as the pull. Start with a light band, this muscle tires fast.

Hamstring curl – Swiss ball, bilateral
3 sets8 repsSwiss ballBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Lie on your back, heels on a Swiss ball, legs straight, hips lifted so the body is in a straight line, arms flat.

Movement: Curl the ball towards the buttocks by bending the knees, keeping the hips lifted, then roll back out under control.

Focus: Keep the hips lifted and level, not dropping, and the ball steady. Keep the core braced, and control the roll back out.

Glute bridge – single leg
3 sets10 repsMatBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg extended straight out and held off the floor.

Movement: Drive through the heel of the bent leg to push your hips up until the body is level. Hold two seconds, then lower slowly under control.

Focus: Keep the hips level, don't let the free side drop or twist. Push with the glute, not the lower back, and keep the ribs down.

For your game: Strong legs and glutes give you the ground force that powers your swing.

Elbow plank
3 sets30 secMatBodyweight
Did something different? Change Sets, Reps or Weight.

Start: Set your forearms on the floor shoulder-width, elbows under the shoulders, legs extended back, toes tucked under.

Movement: Lift the hips to form a straight line from head to heels and hold that position for the set time, breathing steadily.

Focus: Keep a straight line, hips neither sagging down nor piking up, and the core and glutes braced. Keep the ribs down and the neck long, and stop when the line breaks rather than pushing through a drooping back.

For your game: A braced, stable trunk holds your posture and spine angle steady through the swing.

Back squat – BB

Start: Set the bar across the upper back on the traps, hands gripping evenly, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Brace the core hard and unrack, stepping back to a stable stance.

Movement: Sit the hips back and down, bending the knees, until the thighs reach a comfortable depth, keeping the chest up and the bar over mid-foot. Drive up through the heels to stand tall.

Focus: Keep the knees pushed out in line with the middle toes, never caving in, and the heels planted throughout. Keep the chest up and the core braced so the back stays flat, and take depth only to where you keep good form and comfortable knees.

For your game: Strong legs and glutes give you the ground force that powers your swing.

3 x 10 · 15kg
Deadlift – BB

Start: Stand with feet hip-width, the bar over mid-foot. Hinge down to grip just outside your legs, shins to the bar, chest up, back flat, shoulders slightly ahead of the bar, core braced hard.

Movement: Push the floor away and stand tall, keeping the bar dragging close to your legs, hips and shoulders rising together. Finish standing tall with the glutes, then hinge the hips back and lower the bar under control down the same line.

Focus: The back stays flat from floor to lockout, never rounded. Take the load through the legs and hips and keep the bar close to the body throughout. Don't jerk the bar or lean back at the top, just stand tall.

For your game: Hinging from the hips, not the back, is how you hold your posture and load into the ground in the swing.

3 x 8 · 25kg
Chest press – Swiss ball

Start: Lie with the upper back on a Swiss ball, hips up in a bridge, a weight in each hand at chest height, shoulder blades set.

Movement: Press the the weights up until the arms are nearly straight, then lower under control to a comfortable stretch.

Focus: Keep the hips up and the core braced to stay stable on the ball, and the shoulder blades set. Keep the elbows at about 45 degrees, and control the lower.

For your game: Keeping your shoulders and arms in good condition helps you swing freely and without pain.

3 x 8-12 · 2 x 4kg
Hip thrust – single leg

Start: Sit with your upper back against a bench, one foot flat on the floor and roughly under the knee, the other leg lifted and held. Chin tucked, core braced.

Movement: Drive through the planted heel to push the hips up level, squeeze the glute hard at the top, hold briefly, then lower with control.

Focus: Keep the hips level, don't let the free side drop or twist. Finish at a straight line with the glute doing the work, and keep the ribs down so the lower back stays out of it.

For your game: Strong legs and glutes give you the ground force that powers your swing.

Pullover

Movement: Lower the weight back overhead in an arc to a comfortable shoulder stretch, then pull it back over the chest.

Focus: Keep the ribs down and don't arch the lower back as the arms go overhead. Keep the arms fairly straight, go only to a comfortable stretch, and control the arc.

For your game: A strong back is resilient to the forces the swing puts through it, and keeps you comfortable getting round the course.

Pullover – single arm

Movement: Lower the weight back overhead in an arc to a comfortable shoulder stretch, then pull it back over the chest.

Focus: Keep the ribs down and don't let the lower back arch or the body twist as the arm goes overhead. Go only to a comfortable stretch, and control the arc.

For your game: A strong back is resilient to the forces the swing puts through it, and keeps you comfortable getting round the course.

Balance board – soft board

Start: Stand on the soft board on one foot, knee soft, torso tall, with a support within reach.

Movement: Hold steady on the one leg for the set time, making small constant corrections from the foot and ankle. Step off and swap sides between sets.

Focus: Let the ankle and foot do the correcting rather than the arms. Keep the hips level and the standing knee soft, and keep a hand near the support until it settles.

For your game: Soft, uneven ground is what you walk all day on a course, and this teaches the feet to handle it.

Knee flexion – cable

Start: Stand facing a low cable with a cuff around one ankle, holding the frame, torso tall.

Movement: Curl the heel towards the buttock by bending the knee, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the thigh fairly still and move at the knee, curling the heel up. Keep the torso tall and the lower back neutral, and control the lower.

For your game: Keeps your knees strong and comfortable for walking a full round.

3 x 8-12 · 4.25kg
Straight leg raises

Start: Lie on your back, legs straight, hands under the lower back or by the sides, ribs down.

Movement: Raise both straight legs towards the ceiling, then lower them slowly without letting the lower back arch.

Focus: Keep the lower back gently pressed down throughout, and stop lowering the moment it wants to arch. Move slowly, and bend the knees a little if the back lifts.

For your game: A braced, stable trunk holds your posture and spine angle steady through the swing.

Box squat – BB

Start: Set a box behind you at about parallel height. Bar on the upper back, feet shoulder-width or wider, toes out, braced hard.

Movement: Sit the hips back and down to lightly touch the box under control, then drive up through the heels to stand tall. Don't relax fully onto the box.

Focus: Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the shins fairly upright as you sit back. Touch the box under control rather than dropping, and keep the back flat and core braced throughout.

3 x 6-10 · 15kg
Power clean – BB

Start: Stand with a barbell on the floor, feet hip-width, hinged with a flat back, shins near the bar, core braced.

Movement: Drive explosively from the floor through the hips to pull the bar up and catch it at the shoulders in a partial dip, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the back flat as the bar leaves the floor and drive from a sharp hip extension, not arm-pulling. Catch softly with the ribs down and knees tracking over the feet, and control the lower.

3 x 6-10 · 15kg
Romanian deadlift – BB

Start: Stand tall with a barbell held at the front of your thighs, hands just outside your legs, feet hip-width. Set the shoulders back, brace the core hard, and keep a soft bend in the knees.

Movement: Push the hips back and slide the bar down the front of your legs, keeping it in contact, until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings. Keep the knees still and the shins vertical. Drive the hips forward to stand tall and finish with the glutes.

Focus: The back stays flat from start to finish, never rounded. This is a hip hinge, not a squat, so the movement happens at the hips while the bar tracks close to the legs. Only lower as far as you can hold a flat back, and don't lean back or over-arch at the top.

Bulgarian split squat

Start: Stand a stride in front of a bench, the top of your back foot resting on it, torso tall, arms for balance.

Movement: Lower straight down by bending the front knee until the thigh is towards parallel, then drive up through the front heel to the start.

Focus: Keep the front knee tracking over the foot, not caving in, and most of the weight through the front leg. Keep the torso tall, control the descent, and go only as deep as the front knee stays comfortable.

Overhead press – standing

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, ribs down, glutes and core braced.

Movement: Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are straight, then lower back to the shoulders under control.

Focus: Keep the ribs down and squeeze the glutes so the lower back doesn't arch as you press. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears, and press within a comfortable range.

3 x 8-12 · 2 x 6kg
Pull-ups – neutral grip

Start: Hang from neutral (palms-facing) handles, arms extended, chest up, ribs down.

Movement: Pull yourself up until the chin nears the handles, driving the elbows down, then lower slowly under control.

Focus: Lead with the elbows and keep the shoulder blades drawing down, not shrugging. Control the descent, and keep the body still rather than swinging. Any of these can be done with support: on the assisted pull-up machine, or with a band looped over the bar and a foot or knee in it, until you can manage your own bodyweight.

3 x 8-12 · 50kg
Single leg toe tap – suitcase load

Start: Stand tall on one leg, holding a weight at the side in the hand opposite the standing leg, ribs down, standing knee soft.

Movement: Tap the free toe lightly to the floor in front, then out to the side, then behind, returning to a tall single-leg stance between each. Swap sides halfway through the set.

Focus: Resist the pull towards the weighted side, keeping the hips and shoulders level throughout. Control the tap rather than reaching for the floor, and return to tall and balanced before the next one.

For your game: Steady single-leg control keeps your hips level through the swing and your weight shift repeatable.

To burn each side · 5kg
Ski erg

Start: Stand tall holding the handles overhead, feet hip-width, knees soft, core braced.

Movement: Pull the handles down and back while hinging slightly at the hips, then return under control, repeating in rhythm.

Focus: Drive from the trunk and hips with a flat back, not rounding to pull. Keep the knees soft and the movement smooth, and build the pace gradually.

For your game: Conditioning like this builds the stamina to stay strong and focused over all 18 holes.

Goblet squat – pulse

Start: Hold a weight at the chest, elbows tucked, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

Movement: Squat to a comfortable depth and pulse up and down through a small range at the bottom for the set count, then stand tall.

Focus: Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the heels down through every pulse. Keep the chest up and the weight close, and pulse only within a depth the knees tolerate.

For your game: Strong legs and glutes give you the ground force that powers your swing.

Good mornings – BB (pause)

Start: Bar across the upper back, feet hip-width, soft knees, core braced hard.

Movement: Hinge the hips back with a flat back until you feel the hamstrings, pause for two seconds at the bottom, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

Focus: Hold the flat back through the pause, never let it round. Hinge at the hips, keep a soft knee, and only go as deep as your flat back and hamstring flexibility allow.

Push press – BB

Dips – machine assisted

Movement: Bend the elbows to lower until the upper arms are about parallel, then press back up to straight arms.

Balance – single leg eyes closed

2 x 20s each side · Bodyweight
Calf raises – bent knee

Start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, holding a support, knees soft and bent throughout.

Movement: Press through the balls of the feet and lift the heels, then lower slowly over three seconds. Progress to the edge of a step so the heels can drop below the toes.

Focus: Hold the knee bend the whole way. If the legs straighten as you rise, the work moves up into the bulky calf and away from the deep muscle you are after.

Movement: Pull the foot up towards the shin, using the other hand or foot to help if needed, then lower slowly against the band.

Focus: The lowering is the work. Take three or four seconds and resist the whole way. Because you help the foot up, the band can be heavier than the shin could lift alone.

Deadlift – BB tempo

Start: Set up as for a conventional deadlift, feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot, flat back, chest up, core braced.

Movement: Lift the bar to standing with control, then lower it slowly over three to four seconds down the same close path, keeping tension the whole way.

Terminal knee extension

Start: Stand with a band around the back of one knee anchored in front, a slight bend in that knee, holding a support.

Movement: Straighten the knee fully against the band, squeezing the thigh, then let it bend slightly under control.

Ankle dorsiflexion drill

Start: Half kneel or stand with one foot forward, flat on the floor, toes pointing straight ahead.

Movement: Gently drive the knee forward over the toes, keeping the heel down, to a comfortable stretch at the front of the ankle, then return.

Focus: Keep the heel firmly down and let the knee travel over the toes only to a comfortable range. Move slowly, keep the foot pointing straight, and don't force the stretch.

2 x 8-10 · Bodyweight
Anterior tibialis – toe raises off a step

Start: Stand on a step or box with the heels on the surface and the toes hanging out over the edge. Hold a rail or frame for balance.

Movement: Let the toes lower below the level of the step under control, then pull them up towards the shins as high as they will go.

Focus: This is about range, not load. The edge lets the foot drop below level, which is where the shin has to work hardest and where most people have never trained. Go as low as the ankle allows before pulling back up, and keep the knees straight throughout.

3 x 12 · Bodyweight
Hamstring bridge – feet away

Start: Lie on your back and walk the feet further away than you would for a normal bridge, so the legs are nearly straight with only a soft bend at the knee. Heels pressed down, toes lifted.

Movement: Drive down through the heels and lift the hips until you are in a line from shoulder to knee. Hold for a moment at the top, then lower slowly.

Focus: Moving the feet away is the whole point, because it shifts the work off the glutes and onto the hamstrings. You should feel the back of the thigh clearly rather than the backside. If it cramps, walk the feet back in a few inches and build the distance out over a few weeks instead of forcing the position.

For your game: Strong hamstrings hold your posture over the ball instead of letting you stand up out of the shot.

Atomic push-up – TRX

Start: Hands on the floor, feet in the TRX cradles, body in a straight line, core braced hard.

Movement: Perform a push-up, then at the top draw the knees in towards the chest, extend back out, and repeat.

Focus: Keep the body straight during the push-up, not sagging, and control the knee tuck from the core. Keep the shoulders down, and keep the hips from piking as the knees draw in.

Pendlay row

Focus: Keep the back flat and parallel throughout, never rising or rounding as you pull. Lead with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades, and reset the bar on the floor between reps.

3 x 15 · Bodyweight
Calf raises – single leg

Start: Stand on one foot, the ball of the foot on the floor or a step edge, holding a support for balance.

Movement: Rise up onto the toes as high as you comfortably can, then lower the heel slowly under control.

Focus: Rise and lower slowly and evenly, not bouncing, through the full comfortable range. Keep the ankle tracking straight, not rolling out, and control the lower.

3 x 12 each side · Bodyweight
Glute bridges – single leg

Start: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg extended straight out and held off the floor.

Movement: Drive through the heel of the bent leg to push your hips up until the body is level. Hold two seconds, then lower slowly under control.

Focus: Keep the hips level, don't let the free side drop or twist. Push with the glute, not the lower back, and keep the ribs down.

3 x 10 each side · Bodyweight
Bird-dog – weighted arm

Start: On all fours, a light weight in one hand or a cuff on the wrist, back flat and neutral, core braced.

Movement: Reach the weighted arm and the opposite leg out level with the body, hold briefly, then return and repeat, swapping as set.

Focus: Keep the hips and shoulders square and the back flat, resisting the twist the added weight encourages. Move slowly, and keep the reach to where the neutral spine holds.

3 x 8 each side · 2 x 2kg

Deadlift – sumo BB

Start: Take a wide stance, toes out, bar over mid-foot. Sit the hips back and down to grip inside the legs, arms straight, chest up, flat back, shoulders over the bar.

Movement: Drive through the legs and push the knees out, standing the bar up close to the body until the hips lock out tall. Push the hips back to lower along the same line under control.

Focus: Keep the chest up and the back flat, never rounded. Drive the knees out over the toes and take the effort in the legs and hips. Keep the bar close and don't lean back at the top.

4 x 5-6 · 25kg
Hip thrust – BB

Start: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, a padded barbell across the front of your hips. Feet flat, hip-width, shins vertical when the hips are up. Tuck the chin slightly and brace the core.

Movement: Drive through your heels and push the hips up until the thighs are level and the body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top, hold, then lower with control.

Focus: Finish the lift with the glutes at a straight line, don't over-arch the lower back to gain height. Keep the ribs down and the chin tucked so the movement stays in the hips, not the back. Shins stay roughly vertical at the top.

3 x 10 · 10kg
Incline bench press – BB

Start: Lie on an incline bench, feet planted, shoulder blades pinched back and down, grip a little wider than shoulders, unrack over the upper chest.

Movement: Lower the bar under control to the upper chest, elbows tucked to about 45 degrees, then press back up to straight arms.

Focus: Keep the shoulder blades set back and down and the elbows tucked, not flared, to protect the shoulders. Keep the feet planted, lower under control, and don't bounce the bar.

3 x 8 · 10kg
Bent-over row – BB overhand

Start: Hinge forward with a flat back holding a barbell overhand at arms' length, chest up, hips back, core braced.

Movement: Pull the bar towards the upper abdomen, driving the elbows back and out, then lower under control.

Focus: Keep the back flat and the hinge steady, not rounding or rising. Lead with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades, and keep the shoulders down.

3 x 10 · 10kg
Barbell forward lunge

Start: Rest a barbell across the upper back, feet hip-width, torso tall, core braced.

Movement: Step one foot forward into a lunge, lowering until both knees are bent towards right angles, then drive through the front heel to return to standing.

Focus: Keep the front knee over the ankle, not caving in, and the torso tall with the core braced. Control the descent and drive up through the front heel, keeping the hips level.

3 x 8 each side · 10kg
Calf raises – single leg

Start: Stand on one foot, the ball of the foot on the floor or a step edge, holding a support for balance.

Movement: Rise up onto the toes as high as you comfortably can, then lower the heel slowly under control.

Focus: Rise and lower slowly and evenly, not bouncing, through the full comfortable range. Keep the ankle tracking straight, not rolling out, and control the lower.

3 x 12 each side · Bodyweight
Bird-dog

Start: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat and neutral, core braced.

Movement: Reach the opposite arm and leg out straight until level with the body, hold briefly, then return under control and swap.

Focus: Keep the hips and shoulders square to the floor and the back flat, resisting any twist or sag as the limbs extend. Move slowly, and reach only as far as you keep the neutral spine.

3 x 10 each side · Bodyweight
V-sit ups

Start: Lie on your back, legs straight, arms overhead, ribs down.

Movement: Lift the torso and legs together to meet in a V, reaching towards the feet, then lower under control.

Focus: Lift from the core and keep the neck neutral, not straining the head forward. Lower under control without the back arching, and reduce the range if the back complains.

Balance board – perturbation

Start: Stand on a balance board, knees soft, torso tall, ready for small nudges or self-generated wobbles, near a support.

Movement: Keep the board steady while introducing or absorbing small perturbations, recovering balance each time.

Focus: React from the ankles and keep the knees soft and hips level, recovering smoothly. Stay tall, keep the core engaged, and keep support within reach.

3 x 30s · Bodyweight
Anterior tibialis toe raises

Start: Stand with the back against a wall or sit tall, heels down, toes free to lift.

Movement: Raise the toes and fronts of the feet up towards the shins, then lower under control.

Focus: Move only at the ankles, raising the toes as high as you can, and control the lower. Keep it slow and deliberate, feeling the front of the shin work.

3 x 15 each side · Bodyweight

Back squat – pause

Start: Bar on the upper back, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, core braced hard, standing tall after unracking.

Movement: Sit down to a comfortable depth, pause for two to three seconds holding still, then drive up through the heels to stand.

Focus: Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the heels down through the pause. Keep the chest up and the core braced so the back stays flat, and pause only at a depth you control.

3 x 5 · 15kg
Deadlift – BB

Start: Stand with feet hip-width, the bar over mid-foot. Hinge down to grip just outside your legs, shins to the bar, chest up, back flat, shoulders slightly ahead of the bar, core braced hard.

Movement: Push the floor away and stand tall, keeping the bar dragging close to your legs, hips and shoulders rising together. Finish standing tall with the glutes, then hinge the hips back and lower the bar under control down the same line.

Focus: The back stays flat from floor to lockout, never rounded. Take the load through the legs and hips and keep the bar close to the body throughout. Don't jerk the bar or lean back at the top, just stand tall.

3 x 5 · 20kg
DB chest press – single arm

Start: Lie on a bench, a dumbbell in one hand at chest height, the other arm out for balance, shoulder blades set, core braced.

Movement: Press the dumbbell up until the arm is nearly straight, then lower under control to a comfortable stretch.

Focus: Keep the shoulder blades set and resist the torso twisting towards the free side. Keep the elbow at about 45 degrees, not flared, and control the lower.

2 x burn · 4kg
Barbell hip row

Start: Hinge forward with a flat back holding a barbell at arms' length, chest up, core braced, hips back.

Movement: Pull the bar towards the hips, driving the elbows back, then lower under control while holding the hinge.

Focus: Keep the back flat and the hinge steady throughout, not rising or rounding as you row. Lead with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades, and keep the shoulders down.

3 x 8-10 · 10kg
Bulgarian split squat – BB

Start: Barbell across the upper back, stand a stride in front of a bench with the back foot resting on it, torso tall, core braced.

Movement: Lower by bending the front knee until the thigh is towards parallel, then drive up through the front heel to the start.

Focus: Keep the front knee tracking over the foot, not caving in, and the weight through the front leg with the core braced. Keep the torso tall, control the descent, and go only as deep as the knee stays comfortable.

3 x 8 each · 10kg
Reverse crunches

Start: Lie on your back, knees bent up over the hips, hands by the sides or under the lower back, ribs down.

Movement: Curl the knees towards the chest by lifting the hips slightly off the floor, then lower under control.

Focus: Curl using the lower abdomen to lift the hips, not swinging the legs. Keep the movement small and controlled, and don't let the lower back arch as you lower.

3 x burn
Corkscrews

Start: Lie on your back, legs raised towards the ceiling, hands by the sides or under the hips, ribs down.

Movement: Circle the legs in a controlled corkscrew pattern, lowering and sweeping round, then reverse.

Focus: Move the legs slowly from the core and keep the lower back gently pressed down. Keep the circles small enough that the back stays flat, and control throughout.

3 x burn
Anterior tibialis toe raises

Start: Stand with the back against a wall or sit tall, heels down, toes free to lift.

Movement: Raise the toes and fronts of the feet up towards the shins, then lower under control.

Focus: Move only at the ankles, raising the toes as high as you can, and control the lower. Keep it slow and deliberate, feeling the front of the shin work.

3 x 15 · Bodyweight
Balance board – single leg

Start: Stand on a balance board on one foot, knee soft, torso tall, near a support.

Movement: Keep the board level and steady on one leg, making constant small adjustments, for the set time.

Focus: Keep the standing knee soft and the hips level, adjusting from the ankle. Fix the eyes on a point, keep the core engaged, and keep support within reach.

3 x 30s each · Bodyweight
Single leg box squats

Start: Stand on one leg in front of a box or chair, the other leg extended forward off the floor, arms out for balance.

Movement: Sit the hips back and down on the one leg to lightly touch the box, then drive up through the heel to stand.

Focus: Keep the working knee tracking over the toes, never caving in, and the hips level. Touch the box under control, use a higher box to start, and keep the heel down throughout.
